methods.label: Compare the two area formulas
methods.explanation:
The median of a trapezoid joins the midpoints of its nonparallel sides. Its length is the average of the two base lengths, so a trapezoid with median length \(m\) and altitude \(h\) has area \(mh\).

Let \(h>0\) be the common altitude, measured in inches. The triangle's area is
\[
\frac12\cdot18\cdot h=9h.
\]
Since the trapezoid has the same area, \(mh=9h\). Dividing by the positive altitude gives \(m=9\). The median is therefore \(9\) inches, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses elementary area formulas, the trapezoid median theorem, and division by a positive common height.

needsNewNodes.name: Trapezoid median theorem
needsNewNodes.description: The segment joining the midpoints of a trapezoid's nonparallel sides is parallel to its bases and has length equal to half their sum. Consequently, the trapezoid's area equals its median length times its altitude.
